per_probe.note: final int n = 7; return n; — Java 'final' local binding satisfies non-reassignable requirement.
static long counter = 0L; static final long LIMIT = 100L; at class (module-home) scope.
int v; if(cond){v=5;}else{v=9;} return v; — legal under JLS definite-assignment analysis (JLS §16), no placeholder required.

Java arrays are always default/zero-initialized per JLS §4.12.5; java.base exposes no documented mechanism for genuinely uninitialized bulk storage without sun.misc.Unsafe (undocumented/internal). Substituted default-initialized byte[16] per R9 named-substitution exception for F02.P2.
x += 1; (compound assignment, in-place).
xs.set(1, 42); on an ArrayList<Integer> — in-place element mutation through the existing name.

per_probe.citation: JLS §4.12.4 / §8.4.1: Java local variables of primitive type are plain values with no address-of, pointer, ref, or inout mechanism; two names in one scope cannot denote the same writable primitive local storage without wrapping in a heap object/array, which the rubric's P-a note explicitly disallows as a FULL substitute.
per_probe.reason: N-4 (explicitly named in canonical_task/rubric list of probes for which no fragment is written when unavailable).

per_probe.note: List<Integer> window = Collections.unmodifiableList(xs); — documented non-copying read-only view backed by the original list (java.util.Collections Javadoc).
Object routed through a one-element List and read back; same = (first == second) tests Java reference identity distinctly from equals().
Ordinary call f(x) is trivially expressible; determinacy of the outcome set is scored under metric B/D, not here.

per_probe.citation: JLS §8.4.1: Java method arguments are passed by value (primitives) or reference-copy (objects); there is no ref/out/inout parameter form letting a callee write a caller's scalar primitive local. A mutable wrapper object is explicitly excluded as a FULL substitute by the canonical_task.

int m = Integer.MAX_VALUE; int o = m + 1; return o; — rung (iv) plain operator used; higher rungs unavailable because java.lang.Math has no Optional-returning checked add (Math.addExact throws ArithmeticException rather than returning an optional/error value) and no standard saturating add for int.
rung (ii): int q = (b == 0) ? 0 : a / b; — explicit local guard, standard form; rung (i) unavailable because no Optional-returning checked-division op exists in java.lang/java.util.
boolean eq = s1.equals(s2); — content comparison per String.equals Javadoc.
xs.sort(Collections.reverseOrder()); boolean lt = a < b;
rung (ii): int small = (int) big; — explicit narrowing primitive conversion (JLS §5.1.3); rung (i) unavailable because Math.toIntExact throws rather than returning an optional/error value.
double sum = i + d; — binary numeric promotion implicitly widens i to double per JLS §5.6.2, written with no explicit conversion syntax.
int e = xs.get(i); return e; — throws IndexOutOfBoundsException on out-of-range i, per List.get Javadoc (ordinary trapping form).
List<Integer> part = xs.subList(1,4); — documented view backed by xs, not a copy (List.subList Javadoc).
Optional<Integer> o = Optional.empty(); int n = o.orElse(0);

static int parse_twice(String s){ return 2 * Integer.parseInt(s); } — unchecked NumberFormatException propagates without being handled.
try { n = Integer.parseInt(s); } catch (NumberFormatException e) { n = 0; }

sealed interface Shape permits Circle, Rect {} ; record Circle(double r) implements Shape {} ; record Rect(double w, double h) implements Shape {} ; Shape s = new Circle(2.0); — Java 17+ sealed types give a closed alternative set enforced by the compiler.
per_probe.version_assumption: Assumes JDK >= 17 (sealed classes standardized in JEP 409).

per_probe.note: double area = switch(s) { case Circle c -> Math.PI*c.r()*c.r(); case Rect re -> re.w()*re.h(); }; — exhaustive pattern-matching switch over a sealed type, no default arm, checked by the compiler.
per_probe.version_assumption: Assumes JDK >= 21 (pattern matching for switch standardized in JEP 441).

per_probe.note: Open (non-sealed) interface Shape with area(); Circle/Rect implemented in unit 'shapes'; Tri implemented in a separate compilation unit/package without modifying 'shapes'; dispatched through a Shape-typed reference. Uses the frozen multi-unit recipe for Java.
static <T> T head(List<T> xs){ return xs.get(0); } — called at List<Integer> and List<String>; declared result type is T at each call site (generic method, JLS Chapter 8.4.4).
static <T extends Comparable<T>> T max_of(T a, T b){ return a.compareTo(b) >= 0 ? a : b; } — declaration-site bounded type parameter.
interface Named { String tag(); } classes A, B implement it; List<Named> items = List.of(new A(), new B()); items.get(0).tag() dispatches virtually to A's implementation.
List<Integer> xs = new ArrayList<>(List.of(1,2,3)); int total = xs.stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).sum();
Map<String,Integer> mp = new HashMap<>(); mp.put("a",1); int total = mp.values().stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).sum(); int miss = mp.getOrDefault("b", 0);

try (BufferedReader r = new BufferedReader(new FileReader("data.txt"))) { String text = ...; return text.getBytes().length; } — try-with-resources guarantees close() on every exit path including on read failure (JLS §14.20.3).

Java has no deterministic end-of-lifetime hook; Object.finalize() is deprecated for removal (JEP 421) and never guaranteed to run. Substituted nearest standard construct named by the canonical_task: class Handle implements AutoCloseable with close() incrementing 'released', invoked deterministically once by try-with-resources at scope exit.
System.out.println("x"); — java.lang is implicitly available, no import declaration required.

package util; class Util { public static int pub_add(int a,int b){ return a+b+secret(); } private static int secret(){ return 1; } } ; from Main: Util.pub_add(2,3) == 6; secret() is inaccessible outside Util (private, JLS §6.6.1). Uses the frozen Java multi-unit recipe.

CompletableFuture<Integer> f1 = CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> 20); CompletableFuture<Integer> f2 = CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> 22); int sum = f1.get() + f2.get(); — java.util.concurrent is part of the standard runtime shipped with the frozen javac/java recipe.

AtomicLong counter = new AtomicLong(0); two threads each call counter.incrementAndGet() 1000 times; join both; final value == 2000. java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong Javadoc documents atomic, race-free read-modify-write.

java.lang.foreign (Foreign Function & Memory API, JEP 454) lets Java call the platform C 'abs' via Linker.nativeLinker() with no native glue code and no separate toolchain step, satisfying R7. On the assumed JDK 21 LTS baseline this API ships with the JDK but is a preview feature requiring the --enable-preview compiler/runtime flag beyond the plain javac/java frozen recipe (finalized only in JDK 22, JEP 454). Recorded as a flag-outside-frozen-recipe deviation per P-b.
per_probe.version_assumption: If the actual frozen toolchain is JDK >= 22, this probe is FULL instead of PARTIAL; re-score once the toolchain fingerprint is confirmed.

per_probe.citation: javac/java produce JVM bytecode (.class) run by the JVM, not a native ELF/Mach-O/PE binary; there is no platform symbol table for `nm` to inspect and no documented standard mechanism to export an unmangled C-ABI symbol without a separate native compilation step (JNI requires hand-written/generated C glue built by a separate toolchain, which R7 forbids).
